rationales.The improvement is limited or unimpressi: Not much of an improvement downplays how worthwhile the change is, without necessarily denying any improvement.

The expression says there are many possibilities, without comparing their likelihoods.
rationales.The delay was caused by a known number o: Could have and any number of leave both the cause and its count unsettled.
rationales.There are many possible causes of the de: 'Any number of' is an idiomatic way of saying many possible things; it does not identify the actual cause.

rationales.It emphasizes that no page was left unch: 'Every last page' intensifies completeness: all pages, down to the final remaining one, were checked.
